messages:
kevin: Heads up — AcmeApp reported intermittent SSE streams where clients get a partial event payload, then the connection drops and the EventSource reconnects. Customer says it happens only when going through our ALB+Cloudflare path, but not when they hit the origin IP directly. They sent curl repro + node client traces.

kevin: Repro steps they used:
1) curl -v -N 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-xx&session=abc'
2) Wait ~65s, they see some partial text then connection reset.
3) Client EventSource auto-reconnects and continues.

kevin: Error snippets from their curl: 
* curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset by peer
* And in our ELB logs: upstream_connection_error: connection reset

tara: :eyes: ALB default idle timeout is 60s — streaming that has long quiet intervals will be cut if there are no bytes. Could be the ALB closing idle connection.

kevin: They said payloads are infrequent chunks (small tokens) and sometimes there is a 20–30s gap between chunks. So ALB closing at 60s would still be > gap, but they hit ~65s. Maybe combined with Cloudflare or nginx buffer.

joel: Quick checklist I've seen break SSE: proxy buffering + proxy_read_timeout, HTTP/1.0 bridges, and some CF features that buffer/terminate long-lived connections. For nginx -> proxy_buffering on will hold data until buffer full and then flush which looks like a single big chunk to client. For ALB -> idle timeout. For Envoy -> route timeout/stream_idle_timeout.

ash: Can you paste the curl logs through each hop? Direct origin vs ALB vs CF? That helps isolate.

kevin: Provided these:
- Direct to pod IP: curl -N -> stream continues clean for 10m, EventSource never reconnects.
- To ALB only (bypassing CF): connection closes ~62s, server 504? We have "connection idle timeout" messages in ALB logs.
- To ALB+Cloudflare: connection closes ~65s, client sees partial event then reconnect. CF logs show 524 (origin timeout) in one case.

stream-bot: [automated test] periodic keepalive test -> to /v1/stream -> keepalive bytes every 25s: ok for origin, fails at ALB when keepalive suppressed.

joel: Likely a combination: our server sends small event chunks + occasional keepalives; ALB will close idle connections after its idle timeout if it thinks no data is in-flight; Cloudflare may buffer small responses or translate to HTTP/2 which can interact with ALB timeouts. Also double-proxies (CF -> ALB -> nginx -> upstream) multiply timeout layers.

tara: Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Add a server-side heartbeat: send a comment line ":\n" or a small comment (": keepalive\n\n") every 15s to ensure bytes flow. SSE clients ignore comments but proxies will see traffic.
- For ALB: increase idle timeout to something safely > expected quiet window (e.g., 3600s for long streams) or at least > 120s while we triage.
- For nginx fronting our pods: set proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_read_timeout 3600; proxy_send_timeout 3600.
- For Envoy: set route.timeout to 0s (disable) and set stream_idle_timeout appropriately.
- For Cloudflare: where possible, enable "Origin Keepalive" and if using Cloudflare Workers, use the streaming response path. If on proxied plan, note CF may still buffer — may need to bypass CF for streaming endpoints.

ash: Example nginx config snippet that helped another customer:

```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
  proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
}
```

kevin: We tried turning proxy_buffering off in staging and the reproduction went away when ALB timeout was bumped to 300s. So both pieces were contributing.

joel: Also check our runtime kernel TCP keepalive and load-balancer idle connection reuse. Some ALBs consider connections idle if no complete TCP packet exchange occurs even if there are small TCP segments — explicit keepalives from app layer are more reliable for proxies.

kevin: Customer also saw partial JSON chunking where a JSON object is split across chunks and client-side parser errors if they don't handle incremental chunks. We should document recommended client patterns: either buffer until event delimiter (SSE events use "\n\n") or use streaming JSON where the client can parse incremental tokens.

tara: Follow-ups:
- joel: file an infra ticket to audit ALB idle timeout on prod and staging for streaming-enabled routes.
- ash: update nginx config template for streaming endpoints and add an integration test that simulates long quiet intervals.
- kevin: ask customer to try bypassing Cloudflare (temporary) and confirm behavior. If bypass fixes it, CF is likely buffering/closing.

ash: Small note on Envoy: the config keys are a bit different — set route.timeout: 0 (disable) and route.stream_idle_timeout: removed or set to a large value. Also ensure cluster.connect_timeout is sane.

cf-bot: Cloudflare note: connections proxied through Cloudflare may be subject to 100s idle timeouts depending on plan and HTTP version; streaming via Workers or Argo Tunnels can yield different behavior.

kevin: Customer will try bypass + we will push nginx config change to a canary pool. If that fixes, we'll roll to prod and then follow up with a KB article.

tara: For the KB writeup include: cause summary, per-proxy adjustments (ALB, NLB, nginx, Envoy, Cloudflare), server-side heartbeat example, curl repro steps that show direct vs through-proxy, and a small client snippet showing robust SSE handling (buffer until double newline, handle partial event).

joel: I'll add error log examples to the ticket so SREs can map symptoms to root cause quickly: e.g., "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream", "connection reset by peer" on curl, ALB 'idle timeout' entries, and Cloudflare 524/522 patterns.

kevin: Thanks all — I'll update the thread with customer confirmation once they test. :thumbsup:

ash: :+1: good triage steps.
